notes: FROZEN, daemon=incapable — meta only, no phases, because there is no hermes trace for this scenario's property to assert over. Hermes writes no transcript file; the daemon observes committed rows in the shared SQLite store ($HERMES_HOME/state.db, journal_mode=delete). A no-tool hermes turn commits exactly TWO rows: the crash-resilience user row persisted BEFORE the first LLM call (agent/turn_context.py, _ensure_and_persist), which drives ready→working, and ONE complete assistant row carrying its already-resolved terminal finish_reason at generation end, which drives working→ready. Nothing commits in between: HermesState.append_message is the only production writer of `messages` and performs a single INSERT plus the message_count bump in one transaction, no non-test `UPDATE messages SET …` touches `content` or `message_count`, and the assistant row is only constructed after the API call returns (_build_assistant_message(assistant_message, finish_reason)). The live store corroborates it — 117 rows, assistant finish_reason is 'stop' (29) or 'tool_calls' (29), ZERO NULL/empty. Hermes' incremental output is aggregation + terminal render (auxiliary_client stream=True aggregation, stream_single_writer.py) and never reaches the store. A streaming_window phase here would therefore pin a working dwell over SILENCE rather than over partial flushes, which 2-1_basic-turn already covers — so no phases are written, matching the pi/kiro-cli/codex freezes on this row. The contrast is opencode, the other ProcessOwnedStore adapter and the only reason this is not a transport-class verdict: opencode upserts its assistant text-part row at stream start and updates it at stream end, and its recording shows the intermediate transcript_activity (23:52:07.859936) ahead of the terminal one (23:52:11.632798). Unblocks only if hermes starts persisting incremental assistant content mid-generation with a watcher-visible growth signal — today an in-place content UPDATE would not move message_count and would emit nothing.
